description.p: Cordial loads Roblox's official Android x86-64 engine directly on Linux through a purpose-built runtime: the AOSP bionic linker, a bionic/glibc shim, a JNI VM in place of Android's, and a framework layer that answers the client's calls. No emulator, no container, no virtual machine.

Plugins are ordinary programs in their own processes, and they are granted named capabilities rather than access. There is no script execution, no hooking and no memory access — those are absent from the API rather than disabled, so there is no primitive to re-enable in a fork.
Cordial ships no Roblox code, APK or assets. You supply the Android client yourself.

It is experimental. Signing in, loading an experience and playing it with keyboard and mouse all work, text fields draw what you type, and sound plays. Voice chat does not, and on roughly one launch in three a signed-in client reaches the home screen and freezes; reopening usually works. Install it expecting rough edges.
Private servers can be joined from the Roblox website and from a game's Servers list, and joining a game from a Roblox web page closes the page.
Plugins now apply to a running Cordial without restarting it.
Cordial starts again: a change on Roblox's side had it opening to a grey window. It now fetches the same startup settings the Roblox client itself uses.
ARM64 builds are published alongside x86_64. They have not been tested on real ARM hardware yet.
Starting a second profile while one is already running now shows a warning first and asks you to accept or cancel, because multi-instancing risks a Roblox ban. It only asks once.
The Flatpak has a stable channel that only moves on a tagged release; every install before this one is still on the channel that tracks main and needs a manual move to reach it.

Launching twice in a row works. The crash that killed every launch after the first until you cleared the cache was a race between Cordial's startup and the engine's, not a corrupt cache, and Cordial now waits for the engine to be given its flags before going on.

The camera no longer throws you a half-turn on X11, Join in a game's Servers list opens the server instead of doing nothing, and entering fullscreen rebuilds the display chain once rather than once per animation step.

A Roblox build Cordial was merely pointed at — through the Settings picker, CORDIAL_APK, or Sober's package directory — is now checked against Roblox's signing certificate before it is used, the way a build Cordial downloaded itself always was.
The apt, dnf and pacman repositories now publish from a tagged release rather than from every commit to main, and every binary carries its version, its licence and the project URL.

Voice chat reaches the network: the permission answer is delivered both ways the engine expects, and the microphone is captured through callbacks. Audible speech was confirmed before the last round of hardening, not on these exact bytes, so treat it as new.
Clicking Play in a browser now launches the saved profile for that browser account without showing the picker, and the game window's title bar can be hidden for tiling window managers.
The Version page in Settings lists older Roblox builds the mirror has and can download one. Each is checked against Roblox's signature, and downloading one makes it that profile's build.
Roblox can now ask for the microphone. Voice chat still does not work; the release notes say why.
Closing the game window no longer ends on the crash page. The client was segfaulting on the way out, and now exits cleanly.

Cordial keeps the current Roblox build and the two before it, and Settings has a Version page for going back to one. Roblox refuses old clients eventually, so a pinned build will stop working one day.
A resize glitch and the TaskScheduler crash on a second launch are reported and not yet reproduced. Both are described in the release notes.

The AppImage runs on something other than the machine that built it. It was built on Fedora 44 and eighteen of its bundled libraries came out stamped for a glibc four minor versions above the floor Cordial claims, so the one format whose whole promise is portability ran on the one distribution that did not need it. The build base is now Ubuntu 24.04, and none of the 149 bundled libraries is above the floor.
Cordial also no longer fails to start on the newest Roblox build, which began importing a C library function the generated symbol table did not carry.
The web view still does not work inside the AppImage, and the window still does not appear at all on Wayland compositors other than Mutter. Both are described in the release notes.

Plugins ran and then silently died on any host whose kernel refuses unprivileged user namespaces, because Cordial tested for the sandbox by asking whether bwrap was installed rather than whether it could build a sandbox. It now probes a real one and falls back, saying so, to the permission model and broker it already had.
Also the release 0.13.1 should have been: its native packages built correctly and were attached to nothing, so that release carries a Flatpak alone.

Plugins can run. No package Cordial ships installed or bundled Deno, which plugins are written in, so they could not start on any install that did not already have one. Settings now offers to fetch a pinned interpreter where none is present, and the Arch package depends on it properly.

The AppImage can open a web view again; it bundled WebKit without the helper processes WebKit looks for by absolute path. Fixes a flash of the window background when chat opens, and a plugin consent prompt that asked again every time Settings was opened. The FastFlags editor is syntax-coloured and reports errors as you type, and Discord presence shows a game's own art with a default for games that send none.

Built-in plugins are started. They never were: Cordial looked in the user plugin directory and not the system one, so every plugin it ships was listed, granted and switched on without its process ever being spawned. Discord Rich Presence works as a result, recovers if Discord opens later, carries a game's own presence through BloxstrapRPC, and shows a join button.

Controllers are on by default, with a switch and a fix for a virtual mouse being reported as a pad. New settings for frame pacing, FastFlags and quitting when you leave a game. Plugins can be loaded unpacked from a folder and reload as they are edited.

The Flatpak works. Six separate faults stood between the packaged build and a running client, and every one was invisible from a source build: a linker compiled with PATH_MAX=256 that aborted at load, no access to the Roblox build the setup dialog pointed at, the session being written to disk instead of the keyring, every connection reading as metered, and no accessibility bus.

The application ID changes from org.cordial.Cordial to io.github.luohoa97.Cordial, which is an identifier this project controls. An existing install keeps its old data directory and will look freshly installed. The Flatpak also builds for the first time — it had been asking for a runtime with no GTK4 in it — and the published remote definition can now be added at all.

The app bridge is given the surface and platform parameters it was never handed, and everything Cordial fails to answer is collected into one report at exit. Graphics gains an explicit OpenGL ES option. Ctrl+V pastes into Roblox text boxes. Plugins run inside a kernel sandbox beneath Deno's permissions and the capability broker.

Sound comes out, and the microphone is open only while Roblox is recording. The pointer locks, and the launcher no longer imposes a session length. An earlier 1 fps report is withdrawn: it was the desktop, not the engine.

Keys work inside an experience: the engine wants evdev codes, not Android keycodes. Present mode MAILBOX gives a flat 60 where FIFO gave a variable 35 to 50. The engine cache now invalidates when the Roblox build changes, so a warm start runs the build you installed.

The first release anyone could use. Signing in works and the session persists in the desktop keyring rather than on disk; profiles isolate accounts so two run side by side; a native Wayland backend replaces the blank window; and the plugin brokers do something.
